validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed. No gem.wiki page exists for this row (not in wiki_citations.json), so this was open-web research from scratch, not a citation-rot check. Three separate Egypt Oil & Gas (egyptoil-gas.com) publications, at three different dates with two different author teams, all name this exact pipeline: (1) 'A Guide to the Nile Delta's Oil and Gas Resources' (Feb 2020, Issue 158, by Amina Hussien/Reham Gamal/Tasneem Madi) — its 'NATURAL GAS INFRASTRUCTURE IN THE NILE DELTA' table lists a row 'Alexandria Network -Damanhur' From=Alexandria To=Damanhur Length=45km Diameter=24in (pdftotext of the underlying PDF, line 284-285, confirms the exact text, including the mid-name line-wrap 'Alexandria Network' / '-Damanhur' that explains GEM's odd 'Alexandria Network -Damanhur' spacing -- this is almost certainly where researcher NA copied the name from). (2) 'Egypt's Natural Gas Pipelines: Towards a Regional Transit Hub' (Dec 2023, Issue 204, by Jolly Monsef/Mariam Ahmed/Abdullah Mostafa) -- its Nile Delta table (attributed 'according to Wood Mackenzie') independently repeats the same row: Alexandria Network-Damanhur | Alexandria | Damanhur | 45 km | Capacity '-' (no value given). (3) 'Egypt's Gas Distribution Network: An Intricate Economic Web' (features article, published 2024-07-15) names 'Alexandria Network-Damanhur' among Egypt's 10 main Nile Delta pipelines (Abu Madi-Talkha I&II, Talkha-Tanta-Cairo, Abu Madi-Damietta, Meadia-Damanhur, Alexandria Network-Damanhur, Damanhur-Tanta, Cairo Ring-Port Said Line, Korimat-Al Tebbin, Korimat-Beni Suef) without giving specs. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType='transmission' is reasonable -- it is one of the same cohort of Nile-Delta trunk lines (24in diameter, 45km) explicitly grouped with Talkha-Tanta-Cairo and Damanhur-Tanta as a defined national network, not a small gathering/feeder line; no source contradicts transmission. SPEC: LengthKnown=45km and Diameter=24in/DiameterUnits=in match BOTH source (1) and (2) exactly -- no disagreement found anywhere. Capacity is correctly left BLANK: source (2)'s own table shows '-' for this line's capacity (data genuinely unavailable at the source, not a research gap) -- do not force a number here. Status='operating' and Fuel='Gas' are consistent with all three sources' framing (existing, in-service Nile Delta network); no source suggests under-construction/proposed. LOCATION: StartState/Province=Alexandria, EndPrefecture/District=Damanhur, EndState/Province=Beheira all correct -- Damanhur is the seat of Beheira Governorate, and every source's 'From/To' agrees (Alexandria -> Damanhur). DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: compared against P8077 'Meadia-Damanhur Gas Pipeline' (from Abu Qir Development Area/Damietta area, 50km, 20in, capacity 360 MMcf/d) -- these are NOT the same line. Both source tables (1) and (2) list 'Meadia-Damanhur' and 'Alexandria Network-Damanhur' as two SEPARATE rows with different origins, different lengths (50 vs 45km) and different diameters (20in vs 24in) -- textbook case of two distinct parallel trunks feeding the same Damanhur hub from different directions, matching the project's own heuristic that a same-destination pair with different diameter/length is real parallel infrastructure, not a duplicate. No other roster row plausibly matches this corridor. CAVEAT (why 'confirmed (caveat)' not a clean pass): all three corroborating citations are published by the same outlet, Egypt Oil & Gas -- they are three separate, differently-authored, differently-dated (2020/2023/2024) research pieces (one explicitly sourced to Wood Mackenzie) rather than one wire story reprinted, but the project's independence bar wants genuinely separate ORIGINS, and I could not find a non-Egypt-Oil-&-Gas source (GASCO/EGAS primary document, Wikipedia, another outlet) naming this specific line to fully clear that bar -- WebSearch was unavailable this session (200/200 session quota already exhausted by an earlier subagent) so this could not be pushed further by search; a fresh session could try. Two of the three URLs FAIL scripts/url_verifier.py's automated substring screen ('200 but missing expected: Alexandria, Damanhur') -- this is the documented PDF content false-negative pattern (see url_verifier.py's own docstring): both report URLs are cookie-gated endpoints that serve an HTML interstitial to a plain request and the real inline PDF only via a fuller fetch. I downloaded the actual PDFs directly (curl with a browser UA) and confirmed via pdftotext -layout and direct visual read that the exact matching table rows are present as real text, not images. Recommend treating both as valid despite the automated FAIL, per the tool's own guidance to verify large/redirect-gated PDFs manually. Net: I found nothing wrong with this row -- existence, classification, spec, location and non-duplication all check out -- but call it a caveat rather than a clean high-tier pass because of the single-masthead sourcing.
